newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish state group sets up new property company.
newsitem.headline: Swedish state group sets up new property company.

text.p: Swedish state-owned property group Vasakronan said on Tuesday it had set up a new property company, Stenvalvet, of which it would sell 49 percent to another new company, Stenvalvet Invest AB.

Stenvalvet's properties, which are valued at about five billion crowns, include floor space of around 980,000 square metres. The tenants are mostly government authorities, Vasakronan said in a statement.

Credit Suisse First Boston, Sweden's Allmanna Pensionsfonden Femte Fondstyrelsen and U.S. property and asset management firm Crown NorthCorp have formed a consortium which is the arranger and financier for Stenvalvet Invest AB.
Stenvalvet Invest AB will initially acquire 49 percent of shares in Stenvalvet but has an option to increase this.
"In cooperation with Handelsbanken Markets, Vasakronan invites Swedish and international investors to participate in a bid process to acquire a minority interest in the company," Vasakronan said.
"As a result of this process, a letter of intent has been signed with newly formed Swedish company, Stenvalvet Invest AB."
Since 1995 Vasakronan has pursued a strategy of consolidating its property holdings to 15 prioritised communities. The new company consists of properties outside of these communities.
Vasakronan president Hakan Bryngelson said the partnership with Stenvalvet Invest was seen to be very positive.

"Jointly we intend to establish Stenvalvet as a leading property company providing high-quality commercial accommodation in medium-sized locations throughout Sweden where the majority of the portfolio is located," Bryngelson said in the statement.
